claims.statement: The Machinery Regulation becomes mandatory on 20 January 2027, addresses AI-powered safety and cyber-safety, and makes a person performing a substantial modification the manufacturer for the affected machinery.
Manufacturers must create and retain technical documentation and declarations, and safety-related source code or programming logic may be required by authorities when necessary for compliance checks.

Established software already supports risk assessment, technical files, declarations, templates, standards updates, teamwork, and change tracking, directly overlapping the broad discovery proposition.

Public incumbent pricing places capable CE software in the hundreds to low-thousands of euros per licence or package, with annual maintenance and expert add-ons, setting a concrete budget and substitute benchmark.
Pilz already offers end-to-end conformity assessment support, tests, technical-file compilation, and optional authorised-representative services, so expert-assisted handover is not an empty market.
A PLC/configuration-provenance connector may remain differentiated, but the gathered incumbent pages do not establish that this integration gap exists or is budgeted.

contrary_evidence: Safexpert already advertises change tracking, traceable project histories, teamwork, standards monitoring, templates, and technical-documentation workflows.
CEM4 already covers risk assessment, technical files, standards updates, and report generation at relatively low public prices.
CEDOC combines software, onboarding, and paid machine-safety expert support.
Pilz can deliver the complete CE process and assume an authorised-representative role where appropriate.
Not every retrofit is a substantial modification, and responsibility must be assessed case by case.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: partner with one machinery-safety assessor and one PLC/robotics integrator association, then sell against an observed late-change or owner-acceptance failure; no partner commitment is evidenced.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A path to material founder equity would require productising beyond consulting: roughly 150 integrators at 25000-40000 PLN recurring annual revenue plus review revenue could support a 4-6m PLN revenue business and founder equity above 5m PLN in 6-9 years. The gathered evidence confirms incumbent spend but not achievable customer count, switching, or timing.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly during a narrow pilot, with a qualified machinery-safety contractor owning technical review; this is near the high end of part-time fit
economics.gross_margin_basis: Evidence-refined hypothesis: 55-75% blended margin because safety review, onboarding, and integration remain human-intensive; mature software-only work could be higher
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 12-18 months with five annual integrator subscriptions and one to two managed handovers monthly
economics.pricing: Evidence-refined hypothesis: 9000-24000 PLN annual organisation subscription plus 4000-12000 PLN per managed handover. Incumbent software ranges from hundreds to several thousand euros, constraining an undifferentiated seat price.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each new machine, safety-relevant retrofit, standards update, and later substantial modification can trigger work, but existing tools already sell annual updates and reusable project templates.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Integrator-specific mappings among machine variants, safety functions, PLC version identifiers, tests, and accepted handover evidence could reduce later retrofit effort, but established CE platforms already reuse projects and maintain traceable histories.
fingerprint.customer: Polish automation integrators and SME machine builders repeatedly delivering customised cells or retrofits
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Machinery-safety assessor referrals and embedding in an integrator's existing commissioning checklist, beginning with one narrowly repeatable machine class
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Organisation subscription for as-built provenance and release workflow, plus fixed-fee competent-person review on selected handovers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The integrator pays for the shared project workspace and when a new or substantially modified machine reaches the handover gate
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Late changes to controls, safety logic, components, or owner modifications make the generic design file diverge from the commissioned machine

founder_fit: Data lineage, versioning, and quantitative risk workflows fit the founder's technical strengths.
Wielkopolska and Warsaw provide access to industrial integrators without requiring a public-facing creator strategy.
A channel-led, one-machine-category pilot could be part-time.
The founder has no stated machinery-safety credential and must not make technical safety determinations without a qualified contractor.
Integration and enterprise onboarding may consume more than the preferred part-time capacity until the workflow is standardised.
risks: Safety liability or misleading reliance on automated completeness checks
Failure to distinguish a substantial modification from ordinary maintenance or a non-substantial retrofit
Deep overlap with mature CE software and machinery-safety consultancies
Machine-category variation may defeat reusable templates and integration economics
PLC and safety-program artefacts are sensitive customer intellectual property
Long industrial sales and integration cycles may be incompatible with a part-time founder

structure.commercial_archetype: Commissioning assurance workflow with specialist-review service wedge
structure.control_point: The signed as-built configuration baseline and evidence packet before handover or putting the modified machine into service
structure.critical_dependency: Access to integrator engineering artefacts, a repeatable first machine category, and a provenance integration that incumbents do not already satisfy

thesis: A commissioning-focused layer could bind the exact delivered machine configuration—PLC and safety-program version identifiers, risk-control changes, validation results, drawings, component declarations, and open deviations—to the integrator-to-owner release packet. It would complement competent machinery-safety work and existing CE tools rather than calculate safety or certify conformity. The obligation and repeat trigger are real, especially when a substantial modification makes the modifier a manufacturer, but Safexpert, CEM4, CEDOC, and Pilz already cover much of the documentation, change-management, and expert-service stack. The unproven wedge is automated provenance from engineering artefacts into a signed handover baseline.
title: Commissioned-Configuration Machinery Release File
uncertainties: Most repeatable Polish machine or robot-cell category
Frequency and economic cost of as-built file divergence at handover
Whether Safexpert, CEM4, CEDOC, or integrator PLM tools already ingest the needed version identifiers
Integrator willingness to connect PLC repositories and engineering systems
Referral appetite of safety assessors and acceptable liability allocation
Achievable subscription price and annual number of handovers per target integrator
